research_window.note: Continuous coverage begins at the prior exact boundary. No separate development first published in the 32-minute window cleared the publication threshold; two material September 16 Federal Register omissions were restored without changing their event dates.

dedupe_resolutions.notes: The September 11 notice continues the Executive Order 13224 national-emergency framework for another year. The August 26 record concerns three specific OFAC designations made under that authority; the renewal and target-level sanctions are distinct legal actions and consequences.

Vance's end-times statement was made in a broad faith interview and did not explicitly concern Iran or any particular official act. It remains a distinct governance and risk-framing statement rather than being merged into the Iran/Hormuz war record.

The shared EO 14420 token is intentionally preserved in the grid record's timestamped correction note and source description. The official Federal Register assigns EO 14421 to the August 26 grid order and EO 14420 to the August 10 vaccine order; the records concern distinct events and subjects.

The shared White House fact sheet reports both manufacturer pricing arrangements and Medicare Bridge uptake. One record concerns announced company agreements; the other concerns an administration-reported program measurement.

The August employment release is an independently measured economic outcome. Trump's subsequent trade threat used the report as context but is a distinct presidential risk statement with no implementing instrument; neither record substitutes for the other.

The September 4 orders direct ranching, competition, processing, wolf and labeling actions. The August 26 proclamation separately implemented a temporary lean-beef import quota increase; the instruments and outcome tests are distinct.

The national measles surveillance outcome concerns a vaccine-preventable infectious disease. The August 31 newborn record measures vitamin K nonreceipt, which is not a vaccine and involves a different intervention, population and outcome.

LEG-004706 records the June 22 district-court summary judgment vacating modified SAVE. The new record covers the September 4 appellate refusal to stay that judgment and the expedited merits appeal; both stages remain cross-referenced under the same litigation.

The Central African Republic record covers a second implemented flight to that country. The Guyana record covers the first implemented group under a separate bilateral arrangement, different people and different post-transfer terms.

The Liberia record documents a separate agreement and capacity announcement. The Guyana record documents actual arrival of a different six-person group under a one-year temporary arrangement; neither is a duplicate of the other.

The September 4 record concerns a conditional threat to restrict trade with unspecified deficit countries if the Federal Reserve did not cut rates. The September 7 Bombardier statement names one company, ties U.S. market access to domestic manufacturing and arises in a separate Canada aviation dispute; neither threat had an implementing instrument by its cutoff.
The new record documents a named GSA procurement direction, not another tariff implementation. Tariffs, Bombardier sales threats and schedule eligibility have distinct instruments and consequences.

The September 8 appellate ruling in No. 26-5006 is distinct from the April 2025 DOGE-management account. The latter remains unreviewed and queued for source repair; it is not counted as the same court event.
The Los Tiguerones legal designations and Ecuador assistance package are distinct from the SOUTHCOM vessel-interdiction campaign; the records concern different instruments and outcome tests.

Both records touch immigration status, but the Census proposal concerns decennial apportionment and questionnaire design while the birthright-citizenship record concerns citizenship and permanent residence under a separate order and rule.

LEG-001443 concerns the first-term 2018 termination announcement. The new record concerns a separate 2026 statutory continuation and pending DHS determination; the historical ID and later status remain distinct.

The shared tariff-revenue theme does not make Trump's new conditional $5,000 payment pledge the same event as the earlier court ruling on tariff authority. One is an unfunded campaign proposal; the other is a judicial lifecycle stage.

The payment record uses the August Treasury statement only to test the pledge's asserted funding scale. NAT-2026-09-11-009 independently records the government's complete monthly and fiscal-year-to-date cash-flow measurement; a campaign proposal and an official fiscal outcome remain distinct events.

LEG-004698 records the June 2026 collapse of Minnesota church-protest prosecutions. The new record is a later, separately measured outcome analysis of 167 arrests in Los Angeles, Chicago, Portland and Washington; geography, case set and measurement date differ, and neither record is counted as the other.

Both records concern alcoholic-beverage tariffs, but the new record is a product-specific Irish/EU tariff-removal announcement while the existing record concerns implemented and scheduled Canada measures under separate instruments and dates.

Both records use Executive Order 13902, but NAT-2026-09-04-007 covers Turkish financial institutions, later aviation and proxy-network listings, licenses and a civil settlement. NAT-2026-09-14-005 records a separate OFAC designation of Russia’s VTB Bank under Iran authority with different counterparties and secondary-sanctions consequences.
The Big Bend land-use and statutory-authority lawsuit is unrelated to the Minnesota protest-prosecution record despite a broad litigation token match.

Both records cite Executive Order 14192 only as a deregulatory-policy framework. The September 15 proposal concerns banking organizations' third-party risk management, while NAT-2026-09-03-002 concerns a separate regulatory action with different agencies, requirements and outcome tests.
LEG-004657 records the May injunction against closure and renaming; the new record covers the September board vote, implemented closure, new naming restraint and appeal.
LEG-004686 records the June stay denial and removal of Trump's name; the September record is a later court order and closure decision with separate consequences.
